wget & curl: Web Recon & API Testing

A hands-on practical on downloading files and inspecting web requests with wget and curl in a Kali Linux VM, covering file retrieval, recursive downloads, redirect/header inspection, GET/POST requests and a verbose TLS handshake trace.

wgetcurlKali LinuxHTTP / TLS
PART A

Downloading Files with wget

wget --version
curl --version

curl's protocol list (http, https, ftp, sftp, smtp, imap, telnet...) confirmed it supports far more than just HTTP, unlike wget which focuses on downloading files.

cat index.html.2

The -o / -O lesson

wget -o mypage.html https://example.com/index.html

The file held wget's log messages, not the page. Lowercase -o writes the log; uppercase -O saves the downloaded content.

Duplicate filenames and quiet mode

wget -o custom.html https://example.com/index.html wget -q https://example.com/index.html

-q (quiet mode) printed nothing on screen, exactly as intended.

Recursive download

wget -r -l 2 https://example.com

wget created a folder named after the domain and saved one file — only one link on the page, and wget doesn't follow links to other hosts by default.

wget --limit-rate=100k https://example.com/index.html
PART B

Inspecting Requests with curl

curl http://google.com
curl -I https://google.com
HeaderWhat it told me
server: gwsThe web server software the site reveals, a typical recon finding
x-frame-options: SAMEORIGINOnly same-site pages may embed this in a frame (clickjacking defense)
alt-svc: h3=":443"The server advertises HTTP/3 support
curl -L https://google.com

Saving a response to a file

curl -o page.html https://example.com

GET and POST requests

curl https://httpbin.org/get
curl -X POST -d "username=freeman&password=test123" https://httpbin.org/post

The first attempt used lowercase -x and failed — -x sets a proxy, while -X sets the request method.

Custom User-Agent and verbose mode

curl -A "Mozilla/5.0 (MyTestAgent)" https://httpbin.org/headers
curl -v https://example.com

Verbose mode exposed the full connection: DNS resolution, IPv6 fallback to IPv4, the TLSv1.3 handshake, and a verified Cloudflare-issued certificate for example.com.

Conclusion

This practical covered downloading pages with wget, handling duplicate filenames, recursive downloads and quiet mode, then using curl to read redirects and headers, follow redirects, send GET/POST requests, change the User-Agent, and inspect a TLS handshake in verbose mode. A recurring lesson: small typing details matter — -o vs -O, -x vs -X — and reading the error messages was what led to each fix.
